Members of the Agriculture, Conservation, and Forestry Committee, thank you for the opportunity to present to you today, LD 308, "An Act to Update the Laws Governing the Administration of the Animal Welfare Advisory Council." The current chair of the Animal Welfare Advisory Council, Katie Lisnik, approached me about submitting this bill in order to make her work as chair a little more efficient and less difficult. She is present today and will be able to speak to the bill as well.
This bill proposes changes to the operation and flexibility of the Animal Welfare Advisory Council. Specifically, it:
1. Increases Meeting Frequency: The council would no longer be limited to meeting only once every other month. Instead, the bill gives the council the authority to meet more frequently if necessary, which could help address urgent issues more promptly.
2. Delegation of Duties: The bill would grant the chair of the council the ability to delegate duties to individual council members or subcommittees. This could help streamline the work of the council by distributing tasks more efficiently and allowing for specialized focus on particular areas within animal welfare.
Overall, these changes would make the council more responsive and effective in its role while also allowing the chair to delegate her responsibilities to other members and sub-committees. I hope you will join me in supporting this bill.

RE: Testimony in Support of LD 308 - An Act to Update the Laws Governing the Administration of the Animal Welfare Advisory Council
Senator Talbot-Ross, Representative Pluecker, and other Honorable Members of the Agriculture, Conservation and Forestry Committee:
My name is Katie Lisnik and I am the elected Chair of the Animal Welfare Advisory Council, which was established in 2001 per MRS Title 7, Chapter 717. ANIMAL WELFARE ACT, �3906-C. As a Governor appointed Council, we have had several periods where many seats were vacant, and little occurred during the years of the pandemic. We are pleased to report that we now have only two vacant seats, representing kennels licensed under Section 3923-C and licensed pet shops. A full list of members can be found below, as well as the sectors they represent.
The purpose of this Council is to "advise" the ACF Commissioner on matters pertaining to animal welfare. We have been actively meeting almost monthly since 2022 and are working on a variety of issues to advance animal protections in the legislative arena, as well as at the procedural level with guidance being offered on important functions such as Help Fix ME functions and Animal Control Officer certification requirements and training. Past meeting minutes, reports and recordings can all be found here, along with a conduct pledge, and meeting guidelines for public comment. https://www.maine.gov/dacf/ahw/animal_welfare/awac/index.shtml
We thank Representative Pluecker for bringing this bill forward for your consideration. Drawing language from other similar Councils in Maine, we propose a simple update to allow us to utilize subcommittees to delve into more detailed projects or areas of research than the full Council can conduct during our normal meetings. These subcommittees will still adhere to Maine's Freedom of Access laws by advertising the meetings in advance and offering public access both in person and via the online meeting platform used to hold the meeting.
We believe that this change will allow for greater productivity and progress on important issues relevant to the welfare of animals in Maine. We thank you for your consideration of this bill and urge you to vote Ought to Pass.

Senator Talbot Ross, Representative Pluecker, and members of the Joint Standing Committee on
Agriculture, Conservation and Forestry, I am Ronda Steciuk, Director of the Animal Welfare Program (AWP) within the Bureau of Agriculture, Food and Rural Resources. I am speaking on
behalf of the Department of Agriculture, Conservation and Forestry (DACF) in support of LD 308, "An Act to Update the Laws Governing the Administration of the Animal Welfare Advisory
Council.
Per 7 M.R.S. �3906-C, the Animal Welfare Advisory Council's (AWAC) role is to "review and
advise the commissioner on proposed revisions to the animal welfare laws and rules; assist the commissioner in the continuing implementation and evaluation of the animal welfare laws and rules; review training programs for humane agents and animal control officers. . .; research options for increasing revenue to the Animal Welfare Fund. . .; and advise the commissioner on the other matters related to the animal welfare laws and rules." The Council currently has twelve
appointed members and two vacancies; ten are active, attending at least 75% of meetings. The
Council met ten times in 2024, with an average of nine members in attendance.
AWP relies on the Council's feedback and believes the Council will be better able to provide
meaningful feedback and advice by assigning smaller subcommittees specific subject areas and
tasks.
Thank you for the opportunity to testify. I'm happy to answer questions now and at the work
session.
